summary: The non_gaia version is a Python CrewAI implementation with five specialist agents, matching tools, a sequential crew workflow, and a README that maps closely to the stated requirements. It covers all requirement categories at a structural level, but the implementation is explicitly demonstration-grade with mock tool responses and weak evidence of real external integrations.

findings.description: Apartment search by address is represented by a specialist agent and tool, but the tool uses mock data.
findings.evidence: agents/apartment_search_agent.py:9 states the goal to search for apartments by address; tools/apartment_search_tool.py:12 states it is a mock implementation.

findings.description: Investment research is modeled against government sources, but no real government source integration is implemented.
findings.evidence: agents/investment_agent.py:9 targets planned investments from government sources; tools/investment_info_tool.py:12 says it would connect to government databases in a real system.

findings.description: Opinion collection covers local services and several named review platforms in mock output.
findings.evidence: agents/review_agent.py:9 targets local service reviews; tools/review_collection_tool.py:20, 30, and 40 include Google Reviews, Facebook Community, and Local Forum.

findings.description: Price comparison is represented by a specialist agent and mock comparison tool rather than real offer-service calls.
findings.evidence: agents/price_comparison_agent.py:9 targets similar properties from real estate platforms; tools/price_comparison_tool.py:12 states it would connect to real estate platforms in a real system.

findings.description: A report generation tool exists and composes the apartment, investment, review, and price sections.
findings.evidence: tools/report_generation_tool.py:6-7 define Report Generation Tool; lines 18-33 build and return a report object.

findings.description: The crew is sequential and all tools are assigned, but the report task has no explicit context list tying it to previous task outputs.
findings.evidence: main.py:52-56 assigns tools to agents; main.py:95-110 creates a sequential Crew, while report_task at lines 88-91 has no context parameter.

findings.description: Several functions exceed the judge threshold for large functions.
findings.evidence: main.py:58 run_analysis is 61 lines; tools/price_comparison_tool.py:11 _run is 51 lines; tools/review_collection_tool.py:11 _run is 62 lines.

findings.description: The shell entrypoint hardcodes an OPENAI_API_KEY placeholder instead of relying only on external configuration.
The README is transparent that the implementation uses mock data despite production-grade wording elsewhere.
findings.evidence: README.md:78 says the implementation uses mock data and real APIs/databases would be needed in production.

missing_requirements: Real retrieval from government office sources for planned investments.
Real retrieval from review platforms for nearby services.
Real retrieval from offer services for comparable property prices.
logical_inconsistencies: README.md:60 describes production-grade code, while README.md:78 states the implementation uses mock data.
The report task is expected to summarize all earlier outputs, but the task definition does not explicitly declare those outputs as context.
implementation_risks: The system can produce plausible reports from mock data, which risks being mistaken for real market or neighborhood intelligence.
A placeholder API key in entrypoint.sh encourages configuration drift and insecure deployment practices.
Large task/tool methods make it harder to replace mock responses with real API integrations safely.
